provenance.latencyAndThroughput: Emitted by loadtest/idempotency.js handleSummary from k6's own metrics.
provenance.outcomeCounts: Emitted by the same script from the Idempotent-Coalesced response header.
provenance.rowCounts: NOT measured by k6, which cannot query MySQL. Collected by running SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM warehouse.product against the container after each run, and transcribed here.
provenance.serviceCounters: Read from GET /metrics after each run. These are cumulative per process, not per run, so the final entry is the total across all six.
provenance.tablesTruncated: product and idempotency_key were truncated before every run.

harness.topology: k6, API and MySQL all on one macOS laptop. Load average during the final runs was 5.14/4.40/4.40.
harness.caveat: Comparative numbers between designs on identical hardware, not capacity figures for any of them. Tail latency here is contended by the load generator sharing a machine with the database.
harness.workload: constant-arrival-rate POST /products at 400 rps for 60s; every 4 consecutive iterations share one Idempotency-Key, simulating a double-clicked submit.

workloadCaveat: DUPLICATES=4 makes 75% of requests duplicates by construction. Any '75%' figure below describes the injected workload, not something the system discovered. What the system determines is what happens to those duplicates.

current.design: Coalescing with lease renewal and transactional fencing. Duplicates wait for the leader and receive its recorded response; 409 is not in the contract.

correctness.statement: In every run, rows created equalled the unique idempotency-key count exactly, and COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT name) was 0. No run produced a response outside 200/201.

latency.comment: Tail latency is not stable run to run, and the spread widened across the session as the laptop warmed. The median p99 is the number worth quoting; the range is the number worth admitting.

leaseHealth.comment: Zero steals across 143,689 requests is the lease-renewal fix working. Before renewal was added, a leader slower than its 800ms lease was stolen from, and the replacement could be stolen from in turn.

designA_reject409.description: First implementation. Concurrent duplicates were answered immediately with 409 REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT and the client was expected to retry.

saturationSweep.note: 20s per step. Rows created equalled the unique-key count at every rate, including past the knee.

designA_reject409.whyReplaced: Replaced on instruction, to remove 409 from the client contract. It remains the lower-latency and more stable design.

coalescingBeforeFencing.description: Coalescing with lease steal but no transactional fencing and no lease renewal.
coalescingBeforeFencing.defect: One run produced 5,813 product rows against 5,785 idempotency keys: 28 duplicate products, matching that run's 28 lock steals exactly.
coalescingBeforeFencing.rootCause: A lease shows a leader stopped renewing, never that it stopped working. A slow leader had its key stolen mid-insert, and fencing only the settle stopped it recording a result but not committing its row.
coalescingBeforeFencing.fix: The operation moved inside the leader's transaction, committing atomically with the fenced ownership check. Lease renewal was added afterwards so a live-but-slow leader is not stolen from at all.

pollIntervalSweep.note: 400 rps, 20s per step, measured before lease renewal existed. Polling faster is worse: each waiter issues a SELECT per poll, and hundreds of concurrent waiters saturate the pool and starve the leaders they wait on.
pollIntervalSweep.conclusion: A U-curve with its minimum near a 15ms poll. Pool size mattered far less than interval.

legacyBaseline.target: pre-revamp backend/server.js, verbatim except one added `port` config line
legacyBaseline.reproducible: Every duplicate submit returned 500. Since duplicates are 75% of the injected workload, that is 18,000 of 24,001 requests. The product had in fact been created, so the caller could not tell a duplicate from an outage and retrying was unsafe.
legacyBaseline.notReproducible: Run 1 only: 328.66 rps, 12.9s max latency, 86 responses with no HTTP status, and 21 unique products never created. Three later runs showed none of it. Recorded as an unexplained cold-start artifact and excluded from every headline claim.

headline.whatTheSystemDetermines: Every duplicate submit is absorbed. Across 143,689 requests the database held exactly one row per idempotency key, with zero duplicates and zero responses outside 200/201.
headline.whatTheWorkloadFixes: The 75% duplicate ratio is injected by the test, not discovered. It sets how many requests are duplicates; it says nothing about how well they are handled.
headline.legacyComparison: On the same workload the original server returned 500 for every duplicate, so 75% of requests failed while their writes had actually succeeded.
headline.latency: p99 ranged 23.6-394.9ms over six runs, median 86.6ms. The 409-rejecting design measured 8.2-8.5ms and was markedly more stable, so coalescing cost real tail latency to remove client-side retry logic.
honestCaveats: A waiter that exhausts its 2000ms budget still gets a 504 telling it to retry, so the claim that no client needs retry logic holds for the routine path only, not for degraded mode.
All numbers come from one laptop running the load generator, the API and the database together.
At-most-once applies to work done through the supplied transaction. A side effect outside it would re-run on a steal or a reclaim.
